title: A recursive self-improvement framework for electron microscopy analysis
abstract: arXiv:2611.32325v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Resolving local atomic structures such as defects and interfaces from electron microscopy contrast relies heavily on researcher judgement, leading to low efficiency and subjective standards. Here we present PhyEvo-Mic-RSI, a physics-guided and expert-informed recursive self-improvement framework that turns one-off human corrections into reusable, verifiable capabilities by updating executable operators, parameters and routing rules with versioned inheritance. Given researcher-defined tasks, the system selects analysis paths from image features without expert labels, while testing and inheriting code updates under fixed budgets. Combining physical priors with expert feedback improves atomic point-defect detection over larger models and raises cross-material interface coverage from 5.13% to 72.11% within a 10% area budget. translated_title: 面向电子显微分析的递归自我改进框架
translated_abstract: 从电子显微镜衬度中解析缺陷和界面等局部原子结构高度依赖研究人员的判断，导致效率低下且标准主观。在此，我们提出 PhyEvo-Mic-RSI，一个物理引导、专家参与的递归自我改进框架，它通过带版本继承的方式更新可执行算子、参数和路由规则，将一次性的人工修正转化为可复用、可验证的能力。对于研究人员定义的任务，该系统无需专家标注即可根据图像特征选择分析路径，并在固定预算下测试和继承代码更新。将物理先验与专家反馈相结合，使原子点缺陷检测性能超越了更大的模型，并在10%面积预算内将跨材料界面覆盖率从5.13%提升至72.11%。将该框架适配到来自未见研究的显微图像上，进一步通过对齐最优……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出PhyEvo-Mic-RSI，一个物理引导与专家知识相结合的递归自我改进框架，能将研究人员的一次性人工修正转化为可复用、可验证的图像分析能力，显著提升电子显微图像中原子缺陷检测性能和跨材料界面识别覆盖率。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces PhyEvo-Mic-RSI, a physics-guided, expert-informed recursive self-improvement framework that converts one-off human corrections into reusable, verifiable analysis capabilities, substantially improving atomic defect detection and cross-material interface coverage in electron microscopy images.
